entities.summary: Bruno Walter was a German-born conductor, pianist, and composer. Born in Berlin, he left Nazi Germany in 1933, was naturalised as a French citizen in 1938, and settled in the United States in 1939. He worked closely with Gustav Mahler, conducting the premieres of his Ninth Symphony and Das Lied von der Erde. He held major positions with the Leipzig Gewandhaus Orchestra, New York Philharmonic, Concertgebouw Orchestra, Salzburg Festival, Vienna State Opera, Bavarian State Opera, Staatsoper Unter den Linden and Deutsche Oper Berlin, among others, made recordings of historical and artistic significance, and is widely considered to be one of the great conductors of the 20th century.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a renowned conductor, Bruno Walter played a pivotal role in introducing Gustav Mahler's music to the world, premiering his Ninth Symphony and Das Lied von der Erde. His work with major orchestras across Europe and the United States helped shape the musical landscape of the 20th century.
